lesson.text: Quick memory: what steps does a major scale climb? (Tone, tone, semitone, tone, tone, tone, semitone.) Today: major scales from any note, and key signatures.
Start on any note and climb T T S T T T S to build a major scale. From C you use only white keys; from G, the 7th note lands on a black key: F sharp.
The G major scale is G, A, B, C, D, E, F sharp, G. The F major scale needs a flat instead: F, G, A, B flat, C, D, E, F.
A key is the family of notes a piece uses, taken from its scale. A piece in G major uses G's scale, and G is its home note, where the tune feels finished.
Instead of writing a sharp before every F, music puts a key signature at the start of each line: one sharp on the F line means G major, and one flat on the B line means F major.
No sharps or flats means C major. G major has one sharp and F major has one flat. D major has two sharps: F sharp and C sharp.
Worked example: build D major. From D, a tone to E, a tone to F sharp, a semitone to G, then A, B, C sharp and D. The D major scale is D, E, F sharp, G, A, B, C sharp, D.
Try it in the world: look at the start of any song sheet or music book and find its key signature. Count the sharps or flats and name the key. Next: intervals.

exercises.prompt: Which note of the G major scale is sharp?
exercises.hint: Climb T T S T T T S from G. Which step lands on a black key?
exercises.explain: G, A, B, C, D, E, F sharp, G: the 7th note is F sharp.

exercises.prompt: Listen. This scale starts on C and uses only white keys. Which scale is it?
exercises.hint: Only one major scale uses no black keys.
exercises.explain: C major: C, D, E, F, G, A, B, C, all white keys.

exercises.prompt: A key signature is written at the start of each line of music.
exercises.hint: Look at the stave after the clef.
exercises.explain: True: it comes right after the clef on every line.

exercises.prompt: Which key has no sharps or flats?
exercises.hint: Which scale is all white keys?
exercises.explain: C major has no sharps or flats.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Is this scale major or minor?
exercises.hint: Listen to the third note up from home.
exercises.explain: It is G major: B is 4 semitones above G, a major third, so it sounds bright.

exercises.prompt: Which major key has this key signature?
exercises.hint: One sharp, on the F line.
exercises.explain: One sharp, F sharp, is G major.

exercises.prompt: Which major key has this key signature?
exercises.hint: One flat, on the B line.
exercises.explain: One flat, B flat, is F major.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the F major scale. Which note is the flat one?
exercises.hint: Climb T T S from F: which note must be lower than the white key?
exercises.explain: F, G, A, then a semitone up is B flat. The rest are white keys.

exercises.prompt: How many sharps does D major have?
exercises.hint: Build it from D with T T S T T T S.
exercises.explain: D, E, F sharp, G, A, B, C sharp, D: 2 sharps.

exercises.prompt: Which scale is marked?
exercises.hint: It starts on D. Read the steps: T T S T T T S is major.
exercises.explain: It starts on D and climbs T T S T T T S: D major.

exercises.prompt: Listen: this tune is in a major key.
exercises.hint: Listen for the third note up from its home note, D.
exercises.explain: True: it uses D, F sharp and A; F sharp is 4 semitones above D, so it is major.

exercises.prompt: What is the 4th note of the F major scale?
exercises.hint: Climb from F: tone, tone, semitone.
exercises.explain: Climb from F: a tone to G, a tone to A, then a semitone. A semitone above A is B flat, so the 4th note is B flat, not B.

exercises.prompt: In any major scale, how many semitones is it from the 7th note up to the 8th?
exercises.hint: The last step of T T S T T T S.
exercises.explain: The pattern is T T S T T T S, and its last step, from the 7th note to the 8th, is S: 1 semitone (B up to C in C major).

exercises.prompt: Listen. Which scale is this?
exercises.hint: Its first note is its home note. Is it bright?
exercises.explain: It starts and ends on D and climbs T T S T T T S: D major.

exercises.prompt: Why does D major's key signature have two sharps?
exercises.hint: Build the scale and look for black keys.
choices: its scale needs F sharp and C sharp
exercises.explain: The D major scale is D, E, F sharp, G, A, B, C sharp, D: two sharps.

exercises.prompt: G major uses only the white keys.
exercises.hint: Check its 7th note.
exercises.explain: False: climb from G with T T S T T T S and the 7th note lands on F sharp, a black key.

exercises.prompt: A key signature has three sharps: F, C and G sharp. The major key is a semitone above the last sharp. Which key is it?
exercises.hint: What is a semitone above G sharp?
exercises.explain: A semitone above G sharp is A: A major.

exercises.prompt: Listen. This tune ends on its home note. Which note is home?
exercises.hint: Where does the tune sound finished?
exercises.explain: It rests on G at the end, and it uses F sharp: it is in G major.

exercises.prompt: Match each major key to its key signature.
exercises.hint: Count the sharps or flats each scale needs as it climbs T T S T T T S.
exercises.explain: C major: no sharps or flats. G major: one sharp, F sharp. F major: one flat, B flat. D major: two sharps, F sharp and C sharp.

exercises.prompt: Build the G major scale: put the notes after G in order.
exercises.hint: Climb from G one letter at a time; the 7th note needs a sharp.
exercises.explain: G, then A, B, C, D, E and F sharp, and back to G: tone, tone, semitone, tone, tone, tone, semitone.

exercises.prompt: Sort the notes: in the F major scale, or not?
exercises.hint: Build F major first: F, G, A, then a semitone up, then on with tones to the top.
exercises.explain: F major is F, G, A, B flat, C, D, E, F. So B flat, E and C are in it; B, F sharp and C sharp are not.

exercises.prompt: Build a major scale from A. How many sharps does it need?
exercises.hint: Climb from A with T T S T T T S, and mark every black key you land on.
exercises.explain: A, a tone to B, a tone to C sharp, a semitone to D, then E, a tone to F sharp, a tone to G sharp, and a semitone to A. That is 3 sharps: C, F and G sharp.

exercises.prompt: Sort the major scales: do they need sharps, flats, or neither?
exercises.hint: Build each scale with T T S T T T S, or remember its key signature.
exercises.explain: G, D and A major need sharps: 1, 2 and 3 of them. F major needs one flat, B flat. C major needs neither: all white keys.
